The one page a newcomer meets first, a just-deployed realm, is the case the suite never pins, so breaking the default message or the header keeps it green. Fix: assert Render's output against the default message and header in a case that runs before any Set, or restore the message inside the Render test.

verdicts.tldr: the assertion uses realm state as its own needle, so it holds for any output once the message is empty
verdicts.details: strings.Contains(out, Get()) takes the needle from the same variable Render prints, and Contains is true for every haystack when the needle is empty. Set assigns newMsg with no guard (hello.gno:22), so Set(cross(cur), "") is a reachable state, and hello.gno:29-31 invites the reader to change that initial message. In that state the test the PR is built around passes against output carrying none of the realm's state. It keeps its teeth while the message is non-empty, which is why this is polish and not a Warning. Fix: assert against a fixed expected string instead of Get().

verdicts.verify_by: read .github/workflows/ci.yml:29-34 (unpinned master, go-version: stable) against Makefile:3 `GNO ?= gno`; confirm no pin exists on either side.
verdicts.tldr: local green implies CI green only if both sides hold the same gno, and neither side pins one
verdicts.details: AGENTS.md:23-25 closes "so a green local run means a green CI". The targets cannot drift, which is what the workflow comment claims, but the toolchains can: CI curls the master installer and builds gno at job time under `go-version: stable`, while the Makefile's GNO defaults to whatever the contributor installed whenever they last ran `make install`. This round is the axis moving, the PR body reporting verification on gno master.184+393b6f92a while the toolchain used here is master bbd9b2ffe. The newcomer who trusts the sentence reads a red CI as a bug in their own change. Fix: qualify it, green after a fresh `make install`, and say to re-install when CI disagrees.

verdicts.tldr: the documented value drops the "5s" ufmt copies out after the marker
verdicts.details: doPrintf scans width digits first, so for "%-5s" that scan matches nothing and `verb := sTor[i]` is '-', which falls through the verb switch to the default writing `(unhandled verb: %-)`; the loop then resumes at '5' and copies "5s" out as ordinary text. The documented value is a prefix of the real one, and what it drops is the surprising half: the remainder of the spec leaks into the rendered page. A reader who writes an assertion or a Render golden from AGENTS.md's value gets a mismatch. Fix: state the full value, `(unhandled verb: %-)5s`.
verdicts.evidence: My read of gnolang/gno examples/gno.land/p/nt/ufmt/v0/ufmt.gno in the local checkout at ac586457f: the `digits()` width scan runs before `verb := sTor[i]`, the switch default at :225 writes `"(unhandled verb: %" + string(verb) + ")"`, and the outer loop's non-'%' branch then writes each remaining rune. Finder's run on gno master bbd9b2ffe: `AGENTS.md says "(unhandled verb: %-)", got "(unhandled verb: %-)5s"`. Three shas are in play (ufmt source ac586457f, toolchain bbd9b2ffe, PR body master.184+393b6f92a); the parse order quoted is the same in the source read here.

verdicts.verify_by: run `mawk 'BEGIN{FS=":.*?## "} /^[a-zA-Z_-]+:.*?## /{printf "  %-8s %s\n",$1,$2}' Makefile` and `busybox awk` with the same script; compare against the gawk output.
verdicts.tldr: the help recipe's `.*?` is undefined in POSIX ERE, and the implementations that might reject it are untestable here
verdicts.details: FS and the match pattern both use the lazy quantifier POSIX ERE does not define, on the target .DEFAULT_GOAL makes the first thing anyone runs. Under POSIX-mode gawk the construct folds to a greedy `.*` and the listing is correct, so the failure needs an awk that rejects the quantifier rather than folding it, and neither mawk nor busybox awk exists on this machine. The mechanism is real and unmeasured on the implementations at issue, and the same widely-copied snippet runs on mawk-default distributions, which lowers it further. Fix: only if mawk or busybox reproduces, in which case drop the `?`.
verdicts.evidence: My runs in the head worktree on the recipe's exact script: `awk`, `awk --posix` and `awk --traditional` each print all six targets, rc=0, GNU Awk 5.4.1. `command -v mawk busybox original-awk` finds none, so the two implementations the claim rests on were not exercised. What would confirm: the same script under mawk and busybox awk.
